context: An approval must apply to the exact payload, not only a request ID.
chosenPath: Hash the approved payload and validate before execution.
reason: A stale or tampered payload could execute under a valid approval.
tradeoff: Adds implementation complexity but protects approval integrity.

decision: MCP gateway waits before forwarding mutating calls.
context: A child MCP server should not receive dangerous requests before approval.
chosenPath: Gateway creates an approval request and waits.
tradeoff: Adds latency but proves actual human control before execution.

decision: Treat safe alternatives as an MVP safety requirement.
context: Blocking risky tool calls without guidance creates friction and pushes users around the system.
chosenPath: When blocking a mutating call, suggest safer read-only or approval-first alternatives.
rejectedPath: Only deny the request with a generic error.
reason: A security product is more useful when it guides users toward safer workflows.
tradeoff: Requires better policy messaging, but improves trust and usability.

decision: Prioritize executable contract resolution before strategy tuning.
context: The bot generated signals but did not execute trades reliably.
chosenPath: Diagnose broker-instrument mapping, executable symbols, fallback constraints, and feed freshness.
rejectedPath: Keep tuning strategy scores while execution mapping remains broken.
reason: A trading strategy has no practical value if it cannot map to tradable instruments.
tradeoff: Less exciting than strategy work, but more important for real execution.
